+def apply_merges_linked(ids, merges, inverse):
+    """
+    Same result as apply_merges(ids, merges), in O(n log n) for long inputs.
+    Requires: inverse == {rank: pair for pair, rank in merges.items()} with
+    unique int ranks, all greater than every id in ids (so a pair holding a
+    token r never has rank r itself). The tokens form a linked list over the
+    original positions and a heap holds rank * n + position for every pair;
+    all entries of the smallest rank are taken as one batch and merged left
+    to right (exactly what merge() does to every occurrence of that pair),
+    stale entries are skipped, and new neighbouring pairs are pushed.
+    """
+    n = len(ids)
+    if n < 2:
+        return list(ids)
+    get = merges.get
+    tok = list(ids)
+    tok.append(None) # sentinel "next" of the last token: never equals a pair element
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1))
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1))
+    heap = [r * n + i for i, r in enumerate(map(get, zip(ids, ids[1:]))) if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    push = heappush
+    pop = heappop
+    while heap:
+        key = pop(heap)
+        r = key // n
+        base = r * n
+        lim = base + n
+        batch = [key - base]
+        while heap and heap[0] < lim:
+            batch.append(pop(heap) - base)
+        p0, p1 = inverse[r]
+        for j in batch:
+            if tok[j] != p0:
+                continue # stale: this token was merged already
+            k = nxt[j]
+            if tok[k] != p1:
+                continue
+            tok[j] = r
+            tok[k] = None
+            m = nxt[k]
+            nxt[j] = m
+            i = prv[j]
+            if i >= 0:
+                q = get((tok[i], r))
+                if q is not None:
+                    push(heap, q * n + i)
+            if m < n:
+                prv[m] = j
+                q = get((r, tok[m]))
+                if q is not None:
+                    push(heap, q * n + j)
+    return [t for t in tok if t is not None]
+
